title: מַסֶּכֶת אָבוֹת — פֶּרֶק רִאשׁוֹן
part: Chapter 1 · From Moses to Rabban Simeon ben Gamliel
draftNote: The text follows the Wikisource transcription of the Kaufmann manuscript, apart from the editorial steps named in the source note; the prepared audio is being recorded; a check against the manuscript photographs is still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any mishnah to report a problem.
source: Text: the Kaufmann manuscript of the Mishnah (Budapest, Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, Kaufmann A 50), fols. 169r–173v, from the diplomatic transcription on Hebrew Wikisource (כתב יד קאופמן למשנה/מסכת אבות, CC BY-SA 4.0), which records the work of the later hands. The vowel points are the manuscript's own. Where it leaves a letter of a pointed word bare, the editor has supplied the point, and the mishnah's note lists every such word; words the manuscript leaves wholly unpointed stay unpointed. Reading text: the manuscript as corrected. Letters the manuscript erases are omitted; corrections and additions by later hands, including marginal ones, are printed; marginal variant readings (נ״א) are left out. Words the scribe broke across a line end are rejoined. The scribe's abbreviations are kept, marked with a geresh (׳), and expanded in the glossary. The transcription writes Kaufmann's ḥolam, which sits over the preceding letter, as a dot on that letter; it is given here as an ordinary ḥolam. Mishnayot are numbered as in the standard printed editions; where Kaufmann divides differently, or lacks a mishnah, the note says so. Romanization: simplified, following Modern Israeli pronunciation. Pronunciation convention: Modern Israeli Hebrew applied to Kaufmann's vowels — an admitted choice, since the manuscript's pointing reflects an older Palestinian tradition. Translations made fresh from the Hebrew and Aramaic; no modern translation consulted. Audio: Google Cloud TTS, Modern Israeli Hebrew voice, reading the pointed text; abbreviations are read in full (או׳ as אוֹמֵר, שנ׳ as שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, the divine name as Adonay).
about: Avot, "Fathers", is the tractate of the Mishnah made up of maxims; the rest of the Mishnah is law. It opens with the chain of tradition from Moses at Sinai to the Men of the Great Assembly, then gives the sayings of the sages from the early pairs down to the generation of the Mishnah's editor, Rabbi Judah the Prince. The Mishnah was compiled around 200 CE. Many communities read Avot a chapter at a time on Sabbath afternoons between Passover and Shavuot, and often through the summer, adding a sixth chapter, Kinyan Torah, to make six weeks. Chapters 1–5 here follow a single manuscript, the Kaufmann codex, probably copied in Italy in the eleventh or twelfth century and the best witness to the Mishnah's own Hebrew. It reads differently from the familiar printed text in many small places, and the notes point them out.

sentences.t: מֹשֶׁה קִיבֵּל תּוֹרָה מִסִּינַיִ וּמְסָרָהּ לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ לִזְקֵנִים וּזְקֵנִים לִנְבִיאִים וּנְבִיאִים מְסָרוּהָ לְאַנְשֵׁי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הֵם אָמְרוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים הֱיוּ מְתוּנִין בַּדִּין וְהַעֲמִידוּ תַלְמִידִים הַרְבֵּה וַעֲשׂוּ סִיַיג לַתּוֹרָה:
sentences.tr: Moshe kibel tora mi-Sinay u-mesarah li-Yhoshua, vi-Yhoshua li-zkenim, u-zkenim li-nvi'im, u-nvi'im mesaruha le-anshei khneset ha-gdola. Hem amru shlosha dvarim: heyu metunin ba-din, ve-ha'amidu talmidim harbe, va-asu siyag la-tora.
sentences.l: Moses received Torah from Sinai and handed-it to Joshua, and Joshua to elders, and elders to prophets, and prophets handed-it to the men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: be patient in judgment, and raise-up students many, and make a fence for the Torah.
sentences.i: Moses received the Torah from Sinai and passed it on to Joshua; Joshua to the elders; the elders to the prophets; and the prophets passed it on to the Men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be unhurried in judgment, raise up many students, and make a fence around the Torah.
sentences.n: The opening chain of tradition (shalshelet ha-kabbala). Two verbs carry it and you will see both all chapter: קִבֵּל 'received' and מָסַר 'handed on'. 'Torah' has no article here: it means the teaching as a whole. Mishnaic Hebrew spellings to get used to here: plural -in for -im (מְתוּנִין), and הֱיוּ 'be!' (pl.), whose singular is the Mishnaic הֱוֵי. In Kaufmann the second hand erased a doubled וְהַעֲמִידוּ and restored the final mem of תַּלְמִידִים. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: תּוֹרָה, הַגְּדוֹלָה, מְתוּנִין.

sentences.t: שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַדִּיק הָיָה מִשְּׁיָרֵי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הוּא הָיָה אוֹ׳ עַל שְׁלֹשָה דְבָרִים הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד עַל הַתּוֹרָה וְעַל הָעֲבֹדָה וְעַל גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים:
sentences.tr: Shimon ha-tsadik haya mi-shyarei khneset ha-gdola. Hu haya omer: al shlosha dvarim ha-olam omed: al ha-tora, ve-al ha-avoda, ve-al gmilut ḥasadim.
sentences.l: Simeon the Righteous was of the remnants of the Great Assembly. He was saying: on three things the world stands: on the Torah, and on the service, and on the doing of kindnesses.
sentences.i: Simeon the Righteous was one of the last of the Great Assembly. He used to say: The world stands on three things — on Torah, on the Temple service, and on acts of kindness.
sentences.n: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר, 'he was saying' = 'he used to say' — the Mishnah's formula for a sage's habitual teaching; you will meet it again and again. Here the scribe abbreviates אוֹמֵר to אוֹ׳ (tap it). הָעֲבוֹדָה is the sacrificial worship of the Temple. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: מִשְּׁיָרֵי.
sentences.say: שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַדִּיק הָיָה מִשְּׁיָרֵי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר עַל שְׁלֹשָה דְבָרִים הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד עַל הַתּוֹרָה וְעַל הָעֲבֹדָה וְעַל גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים:

sentences.t: אַנְטִיגִנַס אִישׁ סוֹכוֹ קִיבֵּל מִשִּׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵ׳ אַל תִּהְיוּ כַעֲבָדִים הַמְּשַׁמְּשִׁים אֶת הָרָב עַל מְנַת לְקַבֵּל פְּרַס אֶלָּא הֱיוּ כַעֲבָדִים הַמְשַׁמְּשִׁים אֶת הָרָב עַל מְנַת שֶׁלֹּא לְקַבֵּל פְּרַס וִיהֵא מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם עֲלֵיכֶם:
sentences.tr: Antiginas ish Sokho kibel mi-Shimon ha-tsadik. Hu haya omer: al tihyu ka-avadim ha-meshamshim et ha-rav al menat lekabel pras, ela heyu ka-avadim ha-meshamshim et ha-rav al menat she-lo lekabel pras, vi-hei mora shamayim aleikhem.
sentences.l: Antigonos man of Sokho received from Simeon the Righteous. He was saying: do not be like slaves who serve the master on condition to receive a portion, but be like slaves who serve the master on condition not to receive a portion; and let the fear of Heaven be upon you.
sentences.i: Antigonos of Sokho received the tradition from Simeon the Righteous. He used to say: Do not be like servants who serve their master in order to receive a reward; be like servants who serve their master with no thought of reward. And let the fear of Heaven be upon you.
sentences.n: הָרַב here is the slave's owner. פְּרָס is literally a portion or ration — what a master hands out to his slaves. 'Heaven' (שָׁמַיִם) is the Mishnah's reverent way of saying God. Kaufmann spells the name אַנְטִיגִנַס (Antiginas); the printed texts have אַנְטִיגְנוֹס. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: סוֹכוֹ.
sentences.say: אַנְטִיגִנַס אִישׁ סוֹכוֹ קִיבֵּל מִשִּׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר אַל תִּהְיוּ כַעֲבָדִים הַמְּשַׁמְּשִׁים אֶת הָרָב עַל מְנַת לְקַבֵּל פְּרַס אֶלָּא הֱיוּ כַעֲבָדִים הַמְשַׁמְּשִׁים אֶת הָרָב עַל מְנַת שֶׁלֹּא לְקַבֵּל פְּרַס וִיהֵא מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם עֲלֵיכֶם:

sentences.t: יוֹסֵה בֶן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה וְיוֹסֵה בֵן יוֹחָנָן אִישׁ יְרוּשָ׳ קִיבְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ יוֹסֵה בֶן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה אוֹמֵ׳ יְהִי בֵיתָךְ בֵּית וַועַד לַחֲכָמִ׳ וֶהֱוֵוי מִתְאַבֵּק בַּעֲפַר רַגְלֵיהֶם וְשׁוֹתֶה בְצִמְאָה אֶת דִּבְרֵיהֶם
sentences.tr: Yose ben Yo'ezer ish Tsereida ve-Yose ben Yoḥanan ish Yerushalayim kiblu mimenu. Yose ben Yo'ezer ish Tsereida omer: yehi beitakh beit va'ad la-ḥakhamim, ve-hevei mit'abek ba-afar ragleihem, ve-shote ve-tsim'a et divreihem.
sentences.l: Yose son of Yo'ezer man of Tsereida and Yose son of Yoḥanan man of Jerusalem received from him. Yose son of Yo'ezer man of Tsereida says: let your house be a house of meeting for the sages, and be dusting-yourself in the dust of their feet, and drinking with thirst their words.
sentences.i: Yose ben Yo'ezer of Tsereida and Yose ben Yoḥanan of Jerusalem received the tradition from them. Yose ben Yo'ezer of Tsereida says: Let your house be a meeting place for the sages; sit in the dust at their feet, and drink in their words thirstily.
sentences.n: From here on the sages come in pairs (zugot). Picture students sitting on the ground at the feet of teachers on benches — hence 'the dust of their feet'. הֱוֵי + participle ('be dusting yourself') is how the Mishnah gives an ongoing instruction. The printed editions read מֵהֶם, 'from them'; Kaufmann has מִמֶּנּוּ, 'from him'. Two words are abbreviated: יְרוּשָׁ׳ (Jerusalem) and לַחֲכָמִ׳ (the sages).
sentences.say: יוֹסֵה בֶן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה וְיוֹסֵה בֵן יוֹחָנָן אִישׁ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם קִיבְּלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ יוֹסֵה בֶן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה אוֹמֵר יְהִי בֵיתָךְ בֵּית וַועַד לַחֲכָמִים וֶהֱוֵוי מִתְאַבֵּק בַּעֲפַר רַגְלֵיהֶם וְשׁוֹתֶה בְצִמְאָה אֶת דִּבְרֵיהֶם

sentences.t: יוֹסֵה בֶן יוֹחָנָן אִישׁ יְרוֹשָ׳ או׳ יְהִי בֵיתָךְ פָּתוּחַ לָרְוָוחָה וְיהְיוּ עֲנִיִּים בְּנֵי בֵיתֶךְ וְאַל תַּרְבֵּה שִׂיחָה עִם הָאִשָּׁה: בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ אָמְרוּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּאֵשֶׁת חֲבֵירוֹ מִכָּן אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִ׳ כָּל הַמַּרְבֵּה שִׂיחָה עִם הָאִשָּׁה כשהיא נידה גּוֹרֵם רָעָה עַל עַצְמוֹ וּבָטֵל מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְסוֹפוֹ יוֹרֵשׁ לְגֵיהִנָם:
sentences.tr: Yose ben Yoḥanan ish Yerushalayim omer: yehi beitakh patuaḥ la-revaḥa, ve-yihyu aniyim bnei veitekh, ve-al tarbe siḥa im ha-isha. Be-ishto amru, kal va-ḥomer be-eshet ḥavero. Mi-kan amru ḥakhamim: kol ha-marbe siḥa im ha-isha kshe-hi nida gorem ra'a al atsmo, u-vatel mi-divrei tora, ve-sofo yoresh Gehinam.
sentences.l: Yose son of Yoḥanan man of Jerusalem says: let your house be open to the wide, and let the poor be sons of your house, and do not multiply talk with the woman. About his (own) wife they said (it) — light and heavy about the wife of his fellow. From here the sages said: anyone who multiplies talk with the woman when she is menstruant causes harm to himself, and neglects words of Torah, and his end (is that) he inherits Gehenna.
sentences.i: Yose ben Yoḥanan of Jerusalem says: Let your house be wide open, let the poor be members of your household, and do not talk much with women. They said this of a man's own wife — how much more of another man's wife. Hence the sages said: Whoever talks much with a woman while she is in her impurity brings harm on himself, neglects the words of Torah, and in the end inherits Gehenna.
sentences.n: קַל וָחוֹמֶר, 'light and heavy', is the rabbinic a-fortiori argument: if it holds of the lighter case, all the more of the heavier. The words כְּשֶׁהִיא נִדָּה, 'when she is menstruant', are unvocalized in Kaufmann and are not in the printed editions — a restriction that narrows the saying considerably; whether they belong to the scribe's text or are a later addition cannot be settled from the transcription. Kaufmann begins a new mishnah at בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ; the printed editions keep it all as 1:5.
sentences.say: יוֹסֵה בֶן יוֹחָנָן אִישׁ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אוֹמֵר יְהִי בֵיתָךְ פָּתוּחַ לָרְוָוחָה וְיהְיוּ עֲנִיִּים בְּנֵי בֵיתֶךְ וְאַל תַּרְבֵּה שִׂיחָה עִם הָאִשָּׁה: בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ אָמְרוּ קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּאֵשֶׁת חֲבֵירוֹ מִכָּן אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים כָּל הַמַּרְבֵּה שִׂיחָה עִם הָאִשָּׁה כשהיא נידה גּוֹרֵם רָעָה עַל עַצְמוֹ וּבָטֵל מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְסוֹפוֹ יוֹרֵשׁ לְגֵיהִנָם:

sentences.t: יְהוֹשֻעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָיה וּמַתַּיִי הָאַרְבְּלִי קִיבְּלוּ מֵהֶן יְהוֹשֻעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָיה אוֹמֵ׳ עֲשֵׂה לָךְ רָב וּקְנֵה לָךְ חָבֵר וֶהֱוִי דָן אֶת כָּל הָאָדָן לְכַף זְכוּת
sentences.tr: Yehoshua ben Peraḥya u-Matay ha-Arbeli kiblu mehen. Yehoshua ben Peraḥya omer: ase lakh rav, u-kne lakh ḥaver, ve-hevi dan et kol ha-adam le-khaf zkhut.
sentences.l: Joshua son of Peraḥya and Mattai the Arbelite received from them. Joshua son of Peraḥya says: make for-yourself a master, and acquire for-yourself a companion, and be judging every person toward the pan of merit.
sentences.i: Joshua ben Peraḥya and Mattai the Arbelite received the tradition from them. Joshua ben Peraḥya says: Find yourself a teacher, get yourself a companion, and judge everyone favourably.
sentences.n: 'Toward the pan of merit' pictures a balance-scale: when the evidence about someone is in the balance, tip it toward acquittal. מֵהֶן and הָאָדָן show this manuscript's habit of writing a final nun where the printed texts have mem (מֵהֶם, הָאָדָם) — a feature of Mishnaic Hebrew as it was spoken in Palestine. Kaufmann names the second sage Mattai; the printed editions have Nittai (נִתַּאי).
sentences.say: יְהוֹשֻעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָיה וּמַתַּיִי הָאַרְבְּלִי קִיבְּלוּ מֵהֶן יְהוֹשֻעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָיה אוֹמֵר עֲשֵׂה לָךְ רָב וּקְנֵה לָךְ חָבֵר וֶהֱוִי דָן אֶת כָּל הָאָדָן לְכַף זְכוּת

sentences.t: מַתַּיִי הָאַרְבְּלִי אוֹמֵ׳ הרְחַק מִשָּׁכֵן רַע וְאַל תִּתְחַבַּר לָרָשָׁע וְאַל תִּתְיוֹאַשׁ מִן הַפּוּרְעָנוּת
sentences.tr: Matay ha-Arbeli omer: harḥak mi-shakhen ra, ve-al titḥaber la-rasha, ve-al tityo'ash min ha-pur'anut.
sentences.l: Mattai the Arbelite says: keep-far from a bad neighbor, and do not associate with the wicked, and do not despair of the retribution.
sentences.i: Mattai the Arbelite says: Keep away from a bad neighbour, do not attach yourself to a wicked man, and do not give up belief in retribution.
sentences.n: 'Do not despair of retribution' — do not conclude that punishment will never come, either because the wicked seem to prosper or because it seems far off. The he of הַרְחֵק was added by a later hand after the vocalizer had worked: the pointed letters read the Qal רְחַק, 'keep far'. A doubled וְאַל was erased in the manuscript.
sentences.say: מַתַּיִי הָאַרְבְּלִי אוֹמֵר הרְחַק מִשָּׁכֵן רַע וְאַל תִּתְחַבַּר לָרָשָׁע וְאַל תִּתְיוֹאַשׁ מִן הַפּוּרְעָנוּת

sentences.t: יְהוּדָה בֶן טָבַיִי וְשִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטָח קִיבְּלוּ מֵהֶן יְהוּדָה בֶן טָבַיִי אוֹמֵ׳ אַל תַּעַשׂ עַצְמָךְ כְּעַרְכֵי דַּיָּינִים וּכְשֶׁיּיהְיוּ בַעֲלֵי הַדִּין עוֹמְדִין לְפָנֶיךָ יְהְיו בְעֵינֶיךָ כָרְשָׁעִים וּכְשֶׁנִּפְטָרִים מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְהוּא בְעֵינֶיךָ כַצַדִּיקִים שֶׁקִּיבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶן אֶת הַדִּין
sentences.tr: Yehuda ben Tabay ve-Shimon ben Shataḥ kiblu mehen. Yehuda ben Tabay omer: al ta'as atsmakh ke-orkhei ha-dayanin, u-khshe-yihyu ba'alei ha-din omdin lefanekha yihyu ve-einekha ki-rsha'im, u-khshe-niftarim mi-lefanekha yihyu ve-einekha ka-tsadikim she-kiblu aleihem et ha-din.
sentences.l: Judah son of Tabbai and Simeon son of Shataḥ received from them. Judah son of Tabbai says: do not make yourself like arrangers of judges; and when the owners of the case are standing before you, let them be in your eyes like the wicked; and when they take-leave from before you, let them be in your eyes like the righteous, who have accepted upon themselves the judgment.
sentences.i: Judah ben Tabbai and Simeon ben Shataḥ received the tradition from them. Judah ben Tabbai says: As a judge, do not play the advocate. While the litigants stand before you, regard them both as guilty; once they leave, having accepted the verdict, regard them both as innocent.
sentences.n: עוֹרְכֵי הַדַּיָּנִין are those who 'arrange' a case for the judges — advocates who coach a litigant in what to say. The warning is to a judge not to slip into that role for one side. The manuscript was heavily corrected here: כְּ was added by a second hand and עַ written over an erasure; כְּשֶׁיִּהְיוּ and the first יִהְיוּ were corrected from יהוא, a spelling of the same word that survives uncorrected in the second יְהוּא. Vowel points supplied by the editor where the manuscript leaves a letter bare: עֲלֵיהֶן.
sentences.say: יְהוּדָה בֶן טָבַיִי וְשִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטָח קִיבְּלוּ מֵהֶן יְהוּדָה בֶן טָבַיִי אוֹמֵר אַל תַּעַשׂ עַצְמָךְ כְּעַרְכֵי דַּיָּינִים וּכְשֶׁיּיהְיוּ בַעֲלֵי הַדִּין עוֹמְדִין לְפָנֶיךָ יְהְיו בְעֵינֶיךָ כָרְשָׁעִים וּכְשֶׁנִּפְטָרִים מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְהוּא בְעֵינֶיךָ כַצַדִּיקִים שֶׁקִּיבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶן אֶת הַדִּין

sentences.t: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטָח אוֹמֵ׳ הֱוִוי מַרְבֵּה לַחְקוֹר אֶת הָעֵדִים וֶהֱוִוי זָהִיר בִּדְבָרֶיךָ שֶׁמֵּא מִתּוֹכָן יִלְמְדוּ לְשַׁקֵּר:
sentences.tr: Shimon ben Shataḥ omer: hevei marbe laḥkor et ha-edim, ve-hevei zahir bi-dvarekha, she-ma mi-tokhan yilmedu leshaker.
sentences.l: Simeon son of Shataḥ says: be doing-much to examine the witnesses, and be careful with your words, lest from within them they learn to lie.
sentences.i: Simeon ben Shataḥ says: Examine the witnesses thoroughly, and be careful in how you word your questions, or from them they may learn how to lie.
sentences.n: הֱוֵי מַרְבֶּה + infinitive, 'be doing much to…', is an idiom for doing something thoroughly. מִתּוֹכָן, 'from within them' — Mishnaic -an for biblical -am. A judge's leading questions teach a witness which story will hold up.
sentences.say: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטָח אוֹמֵר הֱוִוי מַרְבֵּה לַחְקוֹר אֶת הָעֵדִים וֶהֱוִוי זָהִיר בִּדְבָרֶיךָ שֶׁמֵּא מִתּוֹכָן יִלְמְדוּ לְשַׁקֵּר:

sentences.t: שְׁמַעְיָה וְאַבְטַלְיוֹן קִיבְּלוּ מֵהֶן שְׁמַעְיָה אוֹמֵ׳ אֱהוֹב אֶת הַמְּלָאכָה וּשְׂנָא אֶת הָרַבָּנוּת וְאַל תִּתְוַודַּע לָרְשׁוּת
sentences.tr: Shema'ya ve-Avtalyon kiblu mehen. Shema'ya omer: ehov et ha-melakha, u-sna et ha-rabanut, ve-al titvada la-rshut.
sentences.l: Shemaya and Avtalyon received from them. Shemaya says: love the work, and hate the mastery, and do not make-yourself-known to the authority.
sentences.i: Shemaya and Avtalyon received the tradition from them. Shemaya says: Love work, hate lording it over others, and do not get yourself known to the government.
sentences.n: הָרְשׁוּת, 'the authority', is the ruling power — in Shemaya's day the Hasmonean court and then Rome. Getting noticed by it was dangerous. In Kaufmann a doubled אֶל was erased, and לָ was written over an erasure (the transcriber thinks it replaced a he).
sentences.say: שְׁמַעְיָה וְאַבְטַלְיוֹן קִיבְּלוּ מֵהֶן שְׁמַעְיָה אוֹמֵר אֱהוֹב אֶת הַמְּלָאכָה וּשְׂנָא אֶת הָרַבָּנוּת וְאַל תִּתְוַודַּע לָרְשׁוּת

sentences.t: אַבְטַלְיוֹן אוֹ׳ חֲכָמִ׳ הִיזַּהֲרוּ בְדִיבְרֵיכֶם שֶׁמֵּא תָחוֹבוּ חוֹבַת גָּלוּת וְתִיגְלוּ לִמְקוֹם הַמַּיִם הרעים וישתו התלמידים הַבָּאִים אַחֲרֵיכֶם וְיַמוּתוּ וְנִמְצָא שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מִתְחַלֵּל:
sentences.tr: Avtalyon omer: ḥakhamim, hizaharu be-divreikhem, she-ma taḥovu ḥovat galut ve-tiglu li-mkom ha-mayim ha-ra'im, ve-yishtu ha-talmidim ha-ba'im aḥareikhem ve-yamutu, ve-nimtsa shem shamayim mitḥalel.
sentences.l: Avtalyon says: sages, be careful with your words, lest you incur the penalty of exile and you are exiled to the place of the bad waters, and the students who come after you drink and die, and it is found (that) the name of Heaven is profaned.
sentences.i: Avtalyon says: Sages, be careful what you say. You may be sentenced to exile, and banished to a place of bad water; the students who follow you there will drink and die, and the name of Heaven will be profaned.
sentences.n: Water is the standard rabbinic image for Torah, so 'bad water' is false or careless teaching: an imprecise word from a teacher becomes, in exile among strangers, the poison his students drink. The words הָרָעִים וְיִשְׁתּוּ הַתַּלְמִידִים are unvocalized in the manuscript, though they belong to the standard text.
sentences.say: אַבְטַלְיוֹן אוֹמֵר חֲכָמִים הִיזַּהֲרוּ בְדִיבְרֵיכֶם שֶׁמֵּא תָחוֹבוּ חוֹבַת גָּלוּת וְתִיגְלוּ לִמְקוֹם הַמַּיִם הרעים וישתו התלמידים הַבָּאִים אַחֲרֵיכֶם וְיַמוּתוּ וְנִמְצָא שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מִתְחַלֵּל:

sentences.t: הֶלֵּל וְשַׁמַּיִ קִיבְּלוּ מֵהֶן הֶלֵּל אוֹ׳ הֱוִוי תַלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּאַהֲרֹן אֹהֵב שָׁלוֹם וְרוֹדֵף שָׁלוֹם אֹהֵב אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת וּמְקָרְבָן לַתּוֹרָה:
sentences.tr: Helel ve-Shamay kiblu mehen. Helel omer: hevei mi-talmidav shel Aharon: ohev shalom ve-rodef shalom, ohev et ha-briyot u-mekarvan la-tora.
sentences.l: Hillel and Shammai received from them. Hillel says: be (of) the students of Aaron — loving peace and pursuing peace, loving people and bringing-them-near to the Torah.
sentences.i: Hillel and Shammai received the tradition from them. Hillel says: Be one of Aaron's disciples — loving peace and pursuing peace, loving people and drawing them near to the Torah.
sentences.n: Aaron is the rabbinic model of the peacemaker. בְּרִיּוֹת, literally 'creatures', is the ordinary Mishnaic word for people in general. Kaufmann has תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן, 'a student of Aaron', where the printed editions have מִתַּלְמִידָיו, 'one of his students'; and it writes שֶׁל joined to the next word, as Mishnaic manuscripts usually do.
sentences.say: הֶלֵּל וְשַׁמַּיִ קִיבְּלוּ מֵהֶן הֶלֵּל אוֹמֵר הֱוִוי תַלְמִידוֹ שֶׁלְּאַהֲרֹן אֹהֵב שָׁלוֹם וְרוֹדֵף שָׁלוֹם אֹהֵב אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת וּמְקָרְבָן לַתּוֹרָה:

sentences.t: הוּא הָיָה אוֹ׳ נְגַד שְׁמָא אָבַד שְׁמָא וְדִילָא מוֹסִיף ייסוּף וְדִילָא יְלִיף קְטָלָה חַיָּיב לֹא יעבד קטלה קטלין וְדִי יִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ בְּתָגָא חָלַף
sentences.tr: Hu haya omer: negad shema avad shema, ve-di la mosif yesuf, ve-di la yelif ktala ḥayav, la ya'bed ktala katlin, ve-di yishtamash be-taga ḥalaf.
sentences.l: He was saying: a name spread-abroad, his name is lost; and who does not add will come-to-an-end; and who does not learn deserves death; [not … death … killers]; and who makes-use of the crown passes away.
sentences.i: He used to say: A name made great is a name lost. Whoever does not add to his learning will come to an end. Whoever does not learn deserves death. And whoever makes use of the crown will pass away.
sentences.n: This saying is in Aramaic, the spoken language of Hillel's day — a reminder that Mishnaic Hebrew was a learned language among bilinguals. 'The crown' is the crown of Torah: using one's learning for personal gain. The unvocalized words לֹא יעבד קטלה קטלין are not in the printed editions and their sense is uncertain; they may be a variant or a garbled doublet of the clause before them. The literal layer leaves them as bare words. Kaufmann reads יְסוּף, 'will come to an end', where the printed texts have יָסֵיף; and וְדִי in the last clause was added in the margin.
sentences.say: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר נְגַד שְׁמָא אָבַד שְׁמָא וְדִילָא מוֹסִיף ייסוּף וְדִילָא יְלִיף קְטָלָה חַיָּיב לֹא יעבד קטלה קטלין וְדִי יִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ בְּתָגָא חָלַף

sentences.t: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמ׳ אֵין אֲנִי מִי לִי וּכְשֶׁאֲנִי לְעַצְמִי מָה אָנִי אִם לֹא עַכְשָׁיו אֵמָּתַי:
sentences.tr: Hu haya omer: ein ani, mi li? U-khshe-ani le-atsmi, ma ani? Im lo akhshav, eimatay?
sentences.l: He was saying: (if) I am not, who is for me? And when I am for myself, what am I? If not now, when?
sentences.i: He used to say: If I am not for myself, who will be for me? And when I am only for myself, what am I? And if not now, when?
sentences.n: Kaufmann's wording is shorter than the familiar one: it lacks אִם and לִי — the printed text reads אִם אֵין אֲנִי לִי מִי לִי. As written here, 'If I am not (there), who is for me?' The idiomatic layer gives the familiar sense, which the second clause confirms.
sentences.say: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר אֵין אֲנִי מִי לִי וּכְשֶׁאֲנִי לְעַצְמִי מָה אָנִי אִם לֹא עַכְשָׁיו אֵמָּתַי:

sentences.t: שַׁמַּי אוֹמֵ׳ עֲשֵׂה תוֹרָתָךְ קְבַע אֱמוֹר מְעַט וַעֲשֵׂה הַרְבֵּה וֶהֱוִוי מְקַבֵּל אֶת כָּל הָאָדָם בְּסֵבֶר פָּנִים יָפוֹת
sentences.tr: Shamay omer: ase toratakh keva, emor me'at va-ase harbe, ve-hevei mekabel et kol ha-adam be-sever panim yafot.
sentences.l: Shammai says: make your Torah fixed; say little and do much; and be receiving every person with an expression of a pleasant face.
sentences.i: Shammai says: Make your study of Torah a fixed practice. Say little and do much. And greet everyone with a cheerful face.
sentences.n: קֶבַע, 'fixed', means set times for study that do not give way to whatever else comes up. Note that it is Shammai, famous in later tradition for strictness, who teaches the warm welcome.
sentences.say: שַׁמַּי אוֹמֵר עֲשֵׂה תוֹרָתָךְ קְבַע אֱמוֹר מְעַט וַעֲשֵׂה הַרְבֵּה וֶהֱוִוי מְקַבֵּל אֶת כָּל הָאָדָם בְּסֵבֶר פָּנִים יָפוֹת

sentences.t: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵ׳ אוֹ׳ עֲשֵׂה לָךְ רָב וְהִיסְתַּלֵּק מִן הַסָּפֵק וְאַל תַּרְבֵּה לְעַשֵׂר עֲמָדוֹת
sentences.tr: Raban Gamliel omer: ase lakh rav, ve-histalek min ha-safek, ve-al tarbe le'aser amadot.
sentences.l: Rabban Gamliel says: make for-yourself a master, and remove-yourself from the doubt, and do not do-much to tithe (by) estimates.
sentences.i: Rabban Gamliel says: Find yourself a teacher, and you will be free of doubt. And do not tithe by guesswork too often.
sentences.n: Tithes are a fixed fraction of produce, so they have to be measured; estimating the amount risks giving too little, which leaves the rest forbidden to eat. Kaufmann spells the word עֲמָדוֹת (ayin for alef; printed אוּמָדוֹת) — this manuscript often interchanges the guttural letters. At the line-end before it the scribe wrote the abbreviation אומ׳, unvocalized: a line-filler anticipating the next word, omitted here.
sentences.say: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר עֲשֵׂה לָךְ רָב וְהִיסְתַּלֵּק מִן הַסָּפֵק וְאַל תַּרְבֵּה לְעַשֵׂר עֲמָדוֹת

sentences.t: שִׁמְעוֹן בְּנוֹ אוֹ׳ כָּל יָמַי גָּדַלְתִּי בֵין הַחֲכָמִ׳ וְלֹא מָצָאתִי לַגּוּף טוֹב אֶלָּא שְׁתִיקָה וְלֹא הַמִּדְרָשׁ הוּא הַעִיקָּר אֶלָּא הַמַּעֲשֶׂה כָל הַמַּרְבֶּה דְבָרִים מֵבִיא חֵטְא
sentences.tr: Shimon bno omer: kol yamay gadalti bein ha-ḥakhamim, ve-lo matsati la-guf tov ela shtika. Ve-lo ha-midrash hu ha-ikar ela ha-ma'ase. Kol ha-marbe dvarim mevi ḥet.
sentences.l: Simeon his son says: all my days I grew-up among the sages, and I did not find for the body (anything) good but silence. And not the study is the main-thing, but the deed. Whoever does-much words brings sin.
sentences.i: His son Simeon says: All my life I grew up among the sages, and I have found nothing better for a person than silence. Study is not the main thing, but practice. Whoever talks a great deal brings on sin.
sentences.n: לַגּוּף, 'for the body', means 'for oneself, for a person'. מִדְרָשׁ here means study and interpretation in general.
sentences.say: שִׁמְעוֹן בְּנוֹ אוֹמֵר כָּל יָמַי גָּדַלְתִּי בֵין הַחֲכָמִים וְלֹא מָצָאתִי לַגּוּף טוֹב אֶלָּא שְׁתִיקָה וְלֹא הַמִּדְרָשׁ הוּא הַעִיקָּר אֶלָּא הַמַּעֲשֶׂה כָל הַמַּרְבֶּה דְבָרִים מֵבִיא חֵטְא

sentences.t: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַמְלִיאֵל אוֹ׳ עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים הָעוֹלָם קַיָּים עַל הַדִּין וְעַל הָאֱמֶת וְעַל הַשָׁלוֹם שנ׳ אֱמֶת וּמִשְׁפַּט שָׁלוֹם שִׁפְטוּ בְּשַׁעֲרֵיכֶם
sentences.tr: Raban Shimon ben Gamliel omer: al shlosha dvarim ha-olam kayam: al ha-din, ve-al ha-emet, ve-al ha-shalom, she-ne'emar: emet u-mishpat shalom shiftu be-sha'areikhem.
sentences.l: Rabban Simeon son of Gamliel says: on three things the world endures: on the judgment, and on the truth, and on the peace; as it is said: truth and judgment of peace judge in your gates.
sentences.i: Rabban Simeon ben Gamliel says: The world endures on three things — on justice, on truth, and on peace; as it is said, 'Render true and peaceable justice in your gates' (Zechariah 8:16).
sentences.n: The chapter ends by answering its own beginning: Simeon the Righteous (1:2) named three pillars the world stands on, and Rabban Simeon names three it endures on. The proof-text, introduced by the abbreviation שנ׳ (שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, 'as it is said'), was added in the margin by a second hand in Kaufmann; the printed editions have it in the text.
sentences.say: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים הָעוֹלָם קַיָּים עַל הַדִּין וְעַל הָאֱמֶת וְעַל הַשָׁלוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אֱמֶת וּמִשְׁפַּט שָׁלוֹם שִׁפְטוּ בְּשַׁעֲרֵיכֶם
